sam: FYI were running a targeted maintenance on the edge-gpu pool (racks e4-e7) tonight 02:30-03:15 UTC. Goal: NIC microcode + small kernel bump to address intermittent TX stalls seen at high concurrency. This will be a rolling, per-rack soft reboot with KV pre-seed and controlled backfill.

lee: Are there dedicated customers on that pool? Any blackout windows?

sam: No dedicated. A handful of pipeline jobs run on shared; low traffic window chosen. Plan to keep 1 rack warm for emergency spill.

priya: Network note  our APAC peering has a provider maintenance window overlapping 02:40-03:00 UTC. We should avoid heavy cross-region failover during that interval. Suggest ordering backfill: local-standby -> local-edge-standby -> cross-region (if needed). Throttle cross-region shift to 8%/min.

oscar: Ops steps Ill run: 
```
1) mark cohorts: e4 canary, then e5-e7
2) ./fleet cordon --pool edge-gpu --racks e4
3) ./fleet drain --pool edge-gpu --racks e4 --grace 300 --strategy graceful
4) ./ops/kv-seed --pool edge-gpu --rack e4 --timeout 700
5) post-restore: ./trafficctl limit --pool edge-gpu --rate 0.8 --duration 10m
```

priya: Add network sanity check after each rack: `netcheck --peer apac-peering --p95 50ms` and failfast if p95 > 150ms.

sam: Rollback criteria: sustained P99 errors >1% across the rack OR packet drops >0.4% for 5m. Canary e4 will run 10m validation before continuing.

lee: Cost flag: standby backfill will consume ~6 GPU-hours if we use local standby (~$1.05k). If cross-region used estimated extra egress $300. Tagging cost for review.

pos-bot: Scheduled maintenance reminder created for 02:30 UTC. Warnings at 15m and 2m. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/edge-gpu-maint. Pager thresholds set: P95>210ms for 5m OR task eviction rate>0.7% for 10m.

sam: One more: please keep autoscaler aggressive for 15m post-restore (scale at 55% CPU threshold) to absorb burst. Ill post a short postmortem stub after window. Thanks. :thumbsup:
